Week 5 jumps the long run from 9 to 12 mi (+3) right after the step-back, and week 6 adds 14 mi plus the first MP session. Long run and intensity progress together over weeks 4-6.
Week 4 puts a 5K time trial at the end of a step-back week, or early in week 5 next to the week 5 tempo. This undermines recovery and risks a poor test.

Goal MP of 8:51 (3:52) is set before any fitness test, and MP sessions in weeks 6-15 depend on its result. Pace targets in the plan are provisional, and several workouts (tempo, intervals) are not tied to the test result.

Week 12 stacks a 9-mile MP session and a 21-mile long run in the same 46-mile week, with little room for recovery. Week 11 also has a 19-mile long run with a 5-mile MP block just before it, a heavy two-week sequence.
Only 5 running days per week with a 21-mile long run gives no flexibility to spread the load, so easy volume cannot be raised without adding a sixth day.
